According to recent reports, mauricio Pochettino begins where Jose Mourinho finished, and some would suggest that ought to have been the order of succession at Manchester United anyway. But Mourinho’s last match in charge occurred at Anfield. His United lost 3-1 as Liverpool had 36 shots. Six months later, Jurgen Klopp had another notable victory to celebrate, over Pochettino’s Tottenham in the Champions League final.

But a journey along the East Lancs Road for Pochettino’s bow with United has a pertinence for other reasons, and they stretch beyond the regular comparisons between English football’s two most storied clubs. Opposites in some respects, they are akin in others. When Pochettino looks at the home dugout on Sunday, he may see himself: not so much in the mirror as in the past.

Andoni Iraola is 44, a decade younger than Pochettino and is roughly at the point in his managerial career that the Argentinian was 10 years ago; indeed, that was when many felt United should have appointed him, in preference to the more decorated Mourinho.

Sources indicate that some of those similarities could be dismissed as superficial, even if they suggest Iraola was following Pochettino’s path. Each managed in LaLiga before England, then joining a South Coast club; controversially, too, given the English incumbent who had succeeded was ruthlessly sacked to make way for a man deemed more progressive.

According to recent reports, the eventual verdict was that Southampton got an upgrade on Nigel Adkins, as Bournemouth would on Gary O’Neil. Pochettino took Saints to their joint highest finish for 24 years. Iraola recorded the best in Bournemouth’s history.

Each did so while improving players to such an extent that the established elite started buying them in bulk; indeed, Liverpool were to purchase four of Pochettino’s Saints players and, even before hiring Iraola, had taken Milos Kerkez from Bournemouth and shown an interest in Antoine Semenyo.

In a recent development, A reason was that they were playing a brand of football that seemed to equip them for clubs more accustomed to life nearer the top of the table, which in turn reflected the ethos of the managers. Pochettino and Iraola were not prospering by playing underdog football; a high-paced, attacking, ambitious gameplan meant they earned admirers.

Industry observers note that each was an evangelist for a pressing game. Each had learned from one of its great theorists, Marcelo Bielsa, even if Pochettino was more of a disciple while Iraola’s biggest managerial influence was actually Ernesto Valverde.

Industry observers note that parachuting either in to a superpower required a decision to prioritise potential over a proven ability to win trophies, a style of play over experience. Iraola’s only silverware as a coach has come in Cyprus. Ten years ago, and two seasons into Pochettino’s time at Tottenham, he had won nothing, and Mourinho had won everything.

A fundamental difference in thinking between Liverpool and United may have been apparent in some managerial choices. Liverpool sacked a Premier League winner, in Arne Slot, to appoint Iraola. For a time, United sought solace in silverware, in the Champions Leagues Louis van Gaal and Mourinho had claimed, but picked men who were past their best. Then they sought solace in the silverware secured in lesser leagues by Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim, but picked men who became exposed in the Premier League.

Liverpool may be banking on Iraola becoming a trophy-gatherer as a consequence of combining his methods with better players and when freed from a selling club. For much of the last 13 years, United have seemed to look at the manager’s CV to provide a shortcut to success.

It has been revealed that at times, it may have counted against Pochettino. But, as he finally takes charge of United, there is a way in which he represents a role model to Iraola. The Argentinian took the step up to bigger clubs and, without acquiring the medal collection, has offered the evidence he belongs at that level. Will Iraola, even if he does not last at Liverpool?

In a recent development, because others have floundered and dropped down: to clubs with less scrutiny, or expectation about the style of play. Think of David Moyes after United or Roy Hodgson after Liverpool, or some of Pochettino’s successors at Spurs, Nuno Espirito Santo and Thomas Frank among them. In contrast, since Tottenham, Pochettino has managed Paris Saint-Germain and Chelsea and remained a constant in the conversations for high-profile posts.

Industry observers note that for some of the last decade, however, it has been unclear if his career remains on the upward trajectory it definitely was in 2016, as Iraola’s has been in 2026. Ten years ago, Pochettino seemed to have captured the Zeitgeist, perhaps in alliance with Pep Guardiola and Klopp. Now everyone presses, Pochettino is in his mid-fifties and there is a question if he is still the face of modernity.

According to recent reports, liverpool can note their last two Champions League-winning managers, Rafa Benitez and Klopp, were given the job at 44 and 48 respectively. United’s only unqualified success among managerial appointments since Sir Matt Busby, in Sir Alex Ferguson, was 44 when he arrived at Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that now Iraola is 44; a coincidence, perhaps, but the age can seem a sweet spot, offering coaches some experience while being young enough to have a connection with their players, for their ideas to have a freshness and them to exude energy. Pochettino, another smiling Spanish speaker, may glimpse a vision of what he was when he looks at Iraola. But then his test is to show he remains the man for now.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Manchester City have been dealt a multi-billion-pound blow, following their guilty verdict over breaching Premier League rules.

In September, an independent panel ruled that Man City were guilty of over 100 charges of breaking financial rules, with the Premier League confirming the verdict in an official statement.

Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, described the case as “the most significant in Premier League history”, with the league's own statement using the word “sham” five times.

While the Sky Blues face uncertainty on the pitch – including whether or not they will be relegated from the Premier League as a result of a points deduction – there has reportedly been an impact behind the scenes, too.

The Financial Times reports that United States-based investment firm Apollo Global Management have abandoned a $2 billion loan to City owner Sheikh Mansour – worth just over £1.5bn – following the Premier League's verdict.

Talks were ongoing over the arrangement between The City Football Group and the private capital group, who manage more than $1 trillion of assets and have already dealt with the likes of Atletico Madrid and Nottingham Forest previously.

According to the report, “The loan from Apollo would have provided the group, which also owns clubs in Europe, the Americas and Asia, with extra liquidity as well as being used to refinance existing credit facilities, according to people familiar with the matter.”.

Filings at Companies House now indicate that Sheikh Mansour has invested £100m of equity into CFG via his Newton Investment and Development firm, following the Apollo collapse.

City are yet to feel the effects of the Premier League's verdict but have lost the last three matches in the Premier League after opening the season with seven straight wins.

The six-time champions responded to the news of the verdict with an emphatic 3-0 win over Liverpool at Anfield earlier this season, with the Anfield faithful bringing banners calling out their opponents.

Leading stars such as Erling Haaland, meanwhile, have been questioned over their futures, while former Citizens Manuel Akanji and Kyle Walker have both expressed worry that their titles could be revoked.

Manchester City host Fulham this weekend, as Premier League action continues.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

England are a seeded side for the Nations League quarter-finals after topping their group.

The draw for the final eight teams in the 2026-27 Nations League will be on Friday, 20 November at 11:00 GMT.

It will take place at Uefa's headquarters in Nyon, Switzerland and be broadcast on Uefa TV.

England are the only home nation to have made it to the quarter-final stage, however Northern Ireland's draw against Hungary saw them top Group B2 and secure promotion to League A in the 2028-29 tournament.

Scotland will remain in League B following their third-place finish in Group B1, and Wales face a League A/B relegation play-off in March after being consigned to last place in Group A4.

The Republic of Ireland finished second in Group B3 and so will take part in a League A/B promotion play-off in March.

The winners of groups A1-A4 are seeded for the draw, playing the runners-up of other groups in League A.

England have sealed their place in the last eight as Group A3 winners and could face:.

They cannot face A3 runners-up Spain as teams must be drawn against sides from other groups.

The quarter-finals will be played over two legs during the international break between 25-30 March.

Seeded teams get to play the second leg of their quarter-final at home.

Nations that reach the semi-finals can bid those penultimate matches as well as the final.

The remaining dates for the Nations League are:.

Quarter-finals first leg: 25-27 March.

Quarter-finals second leg: 28-30 March.

Semi-finals, third-place play-off and final: 9-13 June.

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

England will play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in March, in a rematch of this summer’s World Cup quarter-final.

Jude Bellingham scored twice in Miami as England came from behind to end Norway’s sensational World Cup run back in July. England’s World Cup came to an end following defeat to Argentina in the semi-finals but Thomas Tuchel’s side are now looking to build on their impressive victory over world champions Spain in Madrid, which saw them top Group A3, by winning the Nations League for the first time.

Industry observers note that but Erling Haaland’s team will be out for revenge after their incredible comeback to beat Denmark secured progress to the two-legged Nations League quarter-finals. Norway needed to beat Denmark in Copenhagen to finish as runners-up in Group A4, but found themselves two goals down inside 15 minutes. They fought back, however, with Haaland’s last-minute penalty sending them through to the quarter-finals for the first time.

According to recent reports, A place in the Nations League Finals, which will be staged in June and at the end of the season, is up for grabs for the winners. There have been reports of the Football Association expressing an interest in hosting the Nations League Finals, which feature the two semi-finals, a third-place match, and the final. Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany have previously hosted the Finals.

England will go to Norway for the first leg on Saturday 27 March 2027, with a kick-off time of 5pm GMT (UK time).

The return leg will then be played at home on Tuesday 30 March 2027, with a kick-off time of 7:45pm GMT.

The Nations League finals are held at the end of the club season and will be played at one venue between 9-13 June 2027. Portugal, Italy, the Netherlands and Germany have previously hosted the Finals, and there have been reports that England would be interested in staging them should Thomas Tuchel’s side reach the final four.

The host country of the Finals is typically involved in the final four, although the Nations League could also allow the FA a test event before hosting Euro 2028 the following summer, with Scotland, Wales and the Republic of Ireland also co-hosts.

Should England progress to the semi-finals, they will play either Jurgen Klopp’s Germany or Belgium, while the other semi-final will see either Spain or France play against Portugal or the Netherlands.

Germany impressively thashed Netherlands 6-0 on the final game of the group phase to leapfrog them in the table and top Group A2, while Belgium won 4-1 against Italy to finish runner-up in Group A2 behind France.

#36544. How to turn impostor syndrome into a superpower

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1679 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

How to turn impostor syndrome into a superpower

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1679 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that impostor syndrome — a fear of being less competent than people think — is common in researchers.
  • In 2021, Kwabena Boahen Asare found himself in at the deep end when he joined a skin cancer laboratory to gain hands-on research experience.
  • Industry observers note that for Asare, who was a first-year undergraduate student at Dartmouth College in Hanover, Upcoming Hampshire, at the time, it was an exciting but daunting prospect.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that impostor syndrome — a fear of being less competent than people think — is common in researchers. Credit: Gandee Vasan/Getty.

In 2021, Kwabena Boahen Asare found himself in at the deep end when he joined a skin cancer laboratory to gain hands-on research experience.

Industry observers note that for Asare, who was a first-year undergraduate student at Dartmouth College in Hanover, Upcoming Hampshire, at the time, it was an exciting but daunting prospect. Not only was he the sole bachelor’s programme student working alongside senior researchers with years of experience under their belts, he was also the only Black person in the lab. Although Asare’s mentor and colleagues were supportive and encouraging, he felt overwhelmed and out of his depth. “There was a steep learning curve,” he notes.

At the time, Asare viewed his struggles as a sign that he didn’t belong in research. This feeling was compounded by the fact that he was surrounded by colleagues who didn’t share his background as a first-generation student from Ghana.

His experience, and those of many like him, is commonly labelled as impostor syndrome — the fear of not being as competent or knowledgeable as other people think, despite objective accomplishments. In a world that often prizes unflinching self-confidence and boldness, impostor syndrome is usually cast as a psychological flaw that the individual needs to ‘fix’. But it can be a natural response to working in a challenging environment or striving towards an ambitious goal, organizational psychologists say.

Impostor syndrome can also be a reaction to systemic bias and exclusion in the workplace, particularly for people from under-represented groups, including women, says Ruchika Malhotra, an inclusion strategist and founder of Candour, a workplace consultancy in Seattle, Washington. The firm advises organizations on strategies to create diverse teams and inclusive cultures. One study1 conducted at universities in the United States found that women who work in scientific fields that particularly value intellectual brilliance are more likely to feel like impostors than are their male colleagues.

How I tackled post-PhD impostor syndrome.

How I tackled post-PhD impostor syndrome.

It has been revealed that much of the discussion about impostor syndrome pathologizes healthy self-doubt and shifts the responsibility onto individuals instead of the environments that exclude and marginalize them in the first place, adds Malhotra. “A lot of the ways that it’s been talked about haven’t been constructive,” she says.

It has been revealed that although it comes with drawbacks, in some situations, impostor syndrome can be beneficial. For instance, it can help people be better prepared and more focused, particularly when they have a long to-do list.

“Impostor thoughts are almost like your superpower when things get pretty overwhelming,” says Basima Tewfik, an organizational psychologist who studies impostor syndrome at Massachusetts Institute of Technology in Cambridge.

Looking back, Asare says that his impostor syndrome prompted him to reflect on why he wanted to become a researcher in the first place. It has also made him more conscious of his resilience, how he needs to improve and when to seek help, as well as giving him more empathy. This has made him better able to support younger students and researchers who are feeling out of place. “It became my strength,” says Asare, who is now an oncology researcher and consultant at Dartmouth Hitchcock Medical Center in Lebanon, Fresh Hampshire.

According to recent reports, impostor syndrome was first described as ‘impostor phenomenon’ in a 1978 paper on high-achieving women2 co-authored by psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes, both then at Georgia State University in Atlanta. They wrote that people who experience this phenomenon “maintain a strong belief that they are not intelligent; in fact they are convinced that they have fooled anyone who thinks otherwise”.

In the decades since, impostor phenomenon has morphed into a syndrome, even though it isn’t a medical diagnosis, nor is it classified as a psychiatric disorder. A review published in 20233 suggests that around 70% of people will feel unworthy of their accomplishments at some point in their lives. These feelings are even more prevalent in academia, with a 2012 study4 finding that as many as 82% of graduate students experience impostor syndrome to at least some degree. This pattern of thinking often affects high achievers and is associated with lower job satisfaction, hindered performance and burnout. Although some studies, including the 2012 paper, suggest that impostor syndrome affects mostly women and people from other groups under-represented in academia, others argue that it arises in specific situations rather than among particular groups. Relatively few studies have investigated whether commonly cited strategies, such as listing one’s accomplishments and accepting compliments from others, are actually effective.

Impostor syndrome has become a catchphrase in popular culture, with dozens of articles, books and courses describing what it is and how people can overcome it. But in the scientific literature, at least, the exact definition of impostor syndrome, or phenomenon, varies widely. This has created a murky picture of what it really is and how it affects people, says Tewfik. “There are a lot of different ways people describe this phenomenon,” she says. The loose definition has made it easy to confuse impostor syndrome, which causes people to make inferences about what other people think of them, with regular self-doubt, which is more of a personal reflection of your own capabilities, according to Tewfik.

‘Maybe I was never meant to be in science’: how impostor syndrome seizes scientist mothers.

‘Maybe I was never meant to be in science’: how impostor syndrome seizes scientist mothers.

According to recent reports, much of the research on impostor syndrome has also used measures that have made it difficult to distinguish from other psychological patterns, such as negative affectivity, a personality trait that is linked to a tendency to experience negative emotions such as fear, anxiety and insecurity, adds Tewfik. This crossover might explain why most studies on impostor syndrome have shown only negative outcomes, such as a lack of career planning and low motivation to lead5. “It’s possible that what we’ve been studying is actually something much more akin to fear,” says Tewfik.

Sources indicate that this overly negative slant is exacerbated by the fact that many workplaces, including academic ones, place too much emphasis on self-confidence, states Tomas Chamorro-Premuzic, an organizational psychologist at University College London. One 2024 study6 found that workers who display confidence are perceived as more competent and dominant, irrespective of their actual ability.

If impostor syndrome hinders a person’s ability to work or form relationships, it’s usually a symptom of a deeper problem or clinical condition, such as an anxiety disorder. But feeling like you’re about to be ‘found out’ before delivering a big presentation, for example, is usually a sign that you’re being challenged or working outside your comfort zone, claims Chamorro-Premuzic. “There is a very healthy degree somewhere that we’re not appreciating,” he adds (see ‘A toolkit for working with impostor syndrome’).

In scientists, impostor thoughts can simply be a by-product of thinking critically and approaching things with a healthy dose of scepticism, claims Samantha Sutton, an independent career coach for scientists in Boston, Massachusetts. It’s also often a natural response to working in a high-achieving, competitive environment or towards an ambitious goal and should be normalized instead of treated as a problem to solve, she adds. “If you’re up against something major, you should be scared,” says Sutton. When she communicates this to her clients, they are often relieved to hear that they don’t need to strive for total self-confidence before taking steps towards their goals. “They realize that nothing is wrong,” adds Sutton.

Latest Update: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared

📅 02 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 18 min read (3586 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theguardian

⏱️ ~18 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer.
  • According to recent reports, bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run?
  • Key ins: Bruno Guimarães (Newcastle, £75m), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa, £51m), Piero Hincapié (Bayer Leverkusen, £45m), Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge, £34m).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer.

According to recent reports, bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons.

Key ins: Bruno Guimarães (Newcastle, £75m), Ezri Konsa (Aston Villa, £51m), Piero Hincapié (Bayer Leverkusen, £45m), Christos Tzolis (Club Brugge, £34m).

Key outs: Leandro Trossard (Besiktas, £15.3m), Jakub Kiwior (Porto, £14.5m), Gabriel Jesus (Barcelona, £8.6m), Fábio Vieira (Hamburg, £7.7m), Christian Nørgaard (Everton, £7m), Ethan Nwaneri (Borussia Dortmund, loan).

Industry observers note that it is all change at Villa and, although a little trepidation is inevitable, a refresh was probably overdue. At the same time, Unai Emery did not want to lose so many key players and Villa’s manager has made clear there is no such thing as a transition season in his eyes. Villa have generated about £300m from the sales of nine players and brought in 10 at a cost of about £250m. Villa have lowered their wage bill and changed the profile of their squad. Zion Suzuki, Ibrahim Mbaye and Johan Manzambi, names on the lips of Villa’s rivals, are particularly exciting signings. Last summer there was concern Villa had gone stale and 12 months ago they ended up fretting on deadline day – Harvey Elliott and Jadon Sancho joined on loan – but there was no such chaos this time. Ben Fisher.

Key ins: Johan Manzambi (Freiburg, £51m), Nicolas Jackson (Chelsea, £47.5m), Ibrahim Mbaye (PSG, £47m), João Gomes (Wolves, £34m), Zion Suzuki (Parma, £30m), Taylor Harwood-Bellis (Southampton, £25m), Matteo Ruggeri (Atlético Madrid, £21.4m), Leon Goretzka (Bayern Munich, free), Aaron Wan-Bissaka (West Ham, loan), Alejandro Garnacho (Chelsea, loan).

Key outs: Morgan Rogers (Chelsea, £117m), Ollie Watkins (Al-Hilal, £51m), Ezri Konsa (Arsenal, £51m), Youri Tielemans (Manchester United, £35m), Donyell Malen (Roma, £21.6m), Lewis Dobbin (Southampton, £9m), Lucas Digne (PSG, £8.5m), Emiliano Martínez (Chelsea, £7.5m), Evann Guessand (Crystal Palace, loan).

In a recent development, the Guardian's daily football game, On the ball, is now live in the app for both iOS and Android. Can you identify the Premier League star from the clues?

Perhaps Bournemouth’s best business was keeping hold of their coveted key players, chiefly Eli Junior Kroupi, Rayan, Alex Scott and Tyler Adams. Bournemouth rejected bids from Chelsea for Scott and stayed true to their plan of resisting offers to give Marco Rose the best chance of succeeding, with the club attempting to juggle European competition and the league for the first time. The arrival of the Portugal centre-back António Silva, 22, from Benfica looks a typically smart replacement for Marcos Senesi, 29. Kroupi’s freak foot injury, which will probably keep him out until November, may have proved a blessing in disguise in terms of retaining the 20-year-old. BF.

Key ins: António Silva (Benfica, £21.4m), Álvaro Rodríguez (Elche, £21.3m), Juanlu Sánchez (Sevilla, £11.1m), Michele Di Gregorio (Juventus, loan).

Key outs: Luis Sinisterra (Cruzeiro, £5.2m), Enes Unal (Getafe, free), Álex Jiménez (Fiorentina, loan), Marcos Senesi (Tottenham, free).

Avoiding a repeat of last year’s upheaval was a major boost. Keith Andrews held on to his best players and made smart additions to a solid squad. Mamadou Sangaré has added quality in midfield since joining from Lens and looks the bargain of the summer. Callum Wilson has brought experience up front after signing on a free and Jaidon Anthony provides cover on the flanks after his £15m move from Burnley. El Hadji-Malick Diouf, signed from West Ham, offers potential at left-back. Jacob Steinberg.

Key ins: Mamadou Sangaré (Lens, £39m), El Hadji Malick Diouf (West Ham, £35m), Jaidon Anthony (Burnley, £15m), Jannik Schuster (Red Bull Salzburg, £14m), Callum Wilson (West Ham, free).

Key outs: Ethan Pinnock (Coventry, £6m), Jordan Henderson (Chelsea, free).

Industry observers note that deadline day deals to bring in the exciting Nigeria forward Femi Azeez from Millwall and the Spanish midfielder Chema Andrés from Stuttgart made it 12 signings in another summer of transition, Azeez’s arrival being revealed almost 12 hours after the window shut. The departures of Jan Paul van Hecke, Carlos Baleba and Carl Rushworth brought in more than £140m as the Brighton model continues to deliver significant profits, although losing last season’s top scorer, Danny Welbeck, to Chelsea for a mere £5m may be the biggest loss if the new striker Promise David cannot bring the goals. EA.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Tuchel may not have planned it this way, but in one night he gave us all the rich history of the England team at once: some glorious attacking football, some self-sabotage defending, a red card, a late siege and a fight.

This was the beguiling story of Spain 2 England 3, an evening that began with the world champions parading the World Cup trophy and ended with 10 Englishmen defending a lead with their last breath. England beat the world champions in Madrid, and for more than 30 minutes including injury time they did so with 10 men, Dan Burn heading the last ball out as per the tradition of a defensive rearguard action.

This was the game that had it all: including a substitute, in Djed Spence, who had already picked up a yellow card on the bench before he came on. It was a coming-of-age performance in goal for James Trafford. So too for Ben White, the 2022 World Cup departee who scored the third and lunged with astonishing effect in the 84th minute to block a Nico Williams shot.

Recent findings suggest that trafford again! 👊🏻 An excellent double save from the Leeds United keeper 🙌 https://t.co/L27oQFQO1J.

According to recent reports, this was a performance good enough to win a World Cup final, never mind Nations League Group A3 – just a shame England neglected to get to that World Cup final in the summer. The fight in question was at half-time as the players came off and White and Fabián Ruiz first tangled and others dived in.

Industry observers note that there was so much to admire. England began the night testing Spain’s first-phase passing to breaking point. They began the second half counter-attacking Spain for two goals from Ezri Konsa and White. Then after Elliot Anderson’s red card, this was a different England. With Trafford in inspired form, they held off the relentless Spain for long enough.

According to recent reports, harry Kane scored his 93rd England goal from the spot and was replaced before the end so that Myles Lewis-Skelly’s energy could give the midfield one more lease of life. By the end, the excitement meant that Kane was unable to take his seat on the bench, and he stood alongside Tuchel in the technical area, cajoling and advising.

England have beaten Spain on Spanish territory in recent times, but it was the nature of this performance, its many qualities when the moment required them, that made it so significant. This was the end of a 43-game unbeaten streak for the European and world champions, and it was ended by an England team in their best form in recent years.

Sources indicate that only three who started this game – Kane, Jude Bellingham and Declan Rice – started the final of Euro 2024, lost to Spain. Tuchel’s pool of talent is deeper than it was for his predecessor but there is also a greater maturity to the way they play. The England manager called it the greatest performance of almost two years in charge “given the circumstances… who we play, where we play” and as ever for England just slightly too late.

Industry observers note that the defeat by Argentina in the semi-final in Atlanta just stings that little bit more when one considers the craft and resilience England demonstrated on this night. They were under the hammer after Anderson threw an arm over the shoulder of Lamine Yamal and was dismissed before Mikel Oyarzabal converted the penalty that followed. “Thirty minutes against Spain in Spain feels like three hours,” Tuchel said, although Spain had a long way back after the blitzing they took at times in the first hour.

According to recent reports, they all had their moments. Anthony Gordon had a strong first half. Morgan Rogers was central to the two goals England scored in the 10 minutes after the break. Anderson demonstrated that he is one of the best midfielders in the world in the hour before his red card. Spain were without Rodri and in his absence his Manchester City successor was in control.

Tuchel encouraged his players to mount a ferocious press against the best first-phase passing team in the world. Brave, but it worked beautifully and for an absorbing opening 10 minutes, Spain looked all at sea. Such was the pressure, the Spain goalkeeper Unai Simón abandoned the usual build-up strategy and introduced his goal-kicks to the halfway line.

It has been revealed that even when Spain finally found their rhythm at the mid-point of the first half, England adapted. It took them a while to manage the discomfort of being denied the ball, and the familiar rapid incursions and switches of play. The counter-attacking switch from the early period pressing Spain in their own area yielded the penalty from which Kane scored the first.

Penalty to England! The referee immediately points to the spot after Harry Kane is brought down 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 https://t.co/WIXQcJafki.

According to recent reports, anderson snapped into Marc Cucurella and played in Kane with a straight pass punched through the Spain lines. With all his cunning, Kane knew that he could not out-sprint Pau Cubarsi, but he could sucker him into a foul which the England captain did expertly before dispatching the penalty.

WHO ELSE?! 🙌 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Harry Kane converts from the spot just before the break. https://t.co/TY3BjmfaFw.

Industry observers note that then in the second half Rogers found space on the right and ran at Cucurella, who was booked after 50 minutes and vulnerable thereafter. It was Rogers’ breakaway down the right, with pace and control that won the corner for the second. Rice’s delivery was on the money and Rogers also managed to step in front of Aymeric Laporte to allow Konsa a free run on to the header.

KONSA!! 🔥 The Arsenal centre-back doubles England's advantage, as the Three Lions lead the world champions 2-0 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸 https://t.co/A0Q6Wwf261.

The third England goal was even better. Rogers burst from the right to the inside, breaking through the lines and then via Kane got it back on the left. The ball speared into Bellingham was taken cleanly by the Real Madrid man, who adjusted and picked out the run of White. This goal was his greatest moment in an England shirt.

"This England team are RUNNING RIOT in Spain" 🤩 👀 They lead the World Cup winners by 3-0 in Madrid!! WOW. https://t.co/2GuDnscRb4.

Industry observers note that it was only another Jarell Quansah error that got Spain back into the game. His mistake allowed Fermin López to play in Yamal for the run in which he was fouled by Anderson for the red card and the subsequent penalty.

Recent findings suggest that quansah is trying to do the hardest thing asked of a centre-half: play the ball out from the back. His red card in Mexico City and his mistake on Thursday against Croatia have not helped. Nevertheless, John Stones had a tricky start in an England shirt and developed into one of the team’s most important figures.

From another breakaway Yamal crossed for the substitute Williams to score Spain’s second. They would push again but England held on.

Thomas Tuchel praised England’s “statement win” that ended Spain’s 43-game unbeaten run and secured top spot ahead of the world champions in the Nations League.

Tuchel and Declan Rice revealed they had both believed England would end Spain’s long unbeaten streak, and their confidence proved well-founded.

Sources indicate that “This was of course a statement victory,” Tuchel remarked. “I’m happy the players felt so confident. I felt it as well. I also had the same belief [that England would win]. I think we felt it from each other.

Sources indicate that “The result followed the performance. I think it was on the highest level in terms of belief, team spirit, togetherness and it was on the highest level football-wise, in all aspects of the game.”.

Tuchel described the nature of England’s win as “the Azteca reloaded” in reference to the World Cup victory over Mexico, but felt the win in Madrid was the best of his reign as head coach.

He said: “Yeah [it was the best performance of his reign so far], given the circumstances and the pressure and the quality and where we played and playing against the reigning world champions. They were unbeaten in 43 games. So putting a performance out there in Madrid, in this environment, that was a very complete performance and the best I’ve had so far.

It has been revealed that “The last half an hour felt like Azteca reloaded, to be honest. Again, it was a beautiful week. The commitment to get better is on the highest level.

Thomas Tuchel will speak openly to England’s players about what they should do if they encounter racism in the Nations League Group 3 decider with Spain.

This is the first time England have faced Spain in Madrid since November 2004 when they were beaten 1-0 in the Santiago Bernabéu, a game that was ravaged by obscene chanting. The nations were supposed to play a fixture in the Spanish capital in 2008, but the Football Association insisted it be moved to Seville instead.

Earlier this year, Spanish supporters brought shame on themselves again after a flurry of anti-Muslim chants marred a friendly against Egypt; they were fined $20,000 by Fifa and must play their next friendly in a partially closed stadium.

There will be a full house in the Wanda Metropolitano on Sunday night, as the reigning world and European champions aim to defend their extraordinary unbeaten run of 43 games, and England head coach Tuchel is adamant the atmosphere will be in keeping with the occasion.

The German has, however, made it clear he and his staff will use their platform before the contest to remind England’s players of the steps they should take if the worst scenario unfolds.

Sources indicate that asked about incidents that had pockmarked this fixture before, Tuchel remarked: “I think I hear it the first time that this happens. I think it’s unacceptable. In any stadium, not even in stadiums, we will never accept racism. We will never be racist towards anyone.

Good evening and welcome to our live coverage of England’s final Nations League Group 3 decider as Thomas Tuchel’s side take on Spain at Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid.

Sources indicate that although both countries are safely through to the quarter-finals, England will seek revenge on Spain, who beat them in the Euro 2024 final and in their previous Nations League face-off on September 26 at Wembley. That day, Luis de la Fuente’s men profited from Harry Kane’s uncharacteristic penalty miss, England’s general wastefulness in front of goal and some seriously lacklustre defending to earn a chaotic 3-2 comeback victory after falling 2-1 behind at half-time.

Recent findings suggest that since that defeat, England have won four successive Nations League fixtures against the Czech Republic and Croatia by an aggregate score of 14-1. Last time out, they beat Croatia on Thursday, earning a 2-1 win as Kane, who became England’s most-capped men’s player with 126 appearances, dispatched a second-half penalty to seal the three points. Spearheaded by the Ballon d’Or holder’s brilliance, England must win this evening in order to overtake Spain and top the group.

And then you can never predict the result in football, never. But it’s important that we show the mindset that you speak of and the spirit, and we will. I’m very confident about that.”.

Meanwhile, fresh from lifting the World Cup in the summer, Spain have a 100% winning record in this season’s Nations League. According to recent reports, we'll be back with the latest headlines out of Germany tomorrow. Bis dann!

Germany dominated neighbor and historic rival the Netherlands in their Nations League quarterfinal match-up at Berlin's Olympic Stadium on Monday evening.

It was the team's sixth game under head coach Jürgen Klopp and the 50th ever between the two sides.

Industry observers note that germany's 5-0 shellacking of the Oranje was their most lopsided victory since 1959, when they won 7-0. In all, Germany have now won 19 of those matches, the Netherlands have won 12, and 18 ended in a draw.

Speaking to German broadcaster ARD after the game, attacking midfielder Florian Wirtz — who scored twice in the fixture — stated: "We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half.".

Despite the loss, Xavi Hernandez's Dutch side will reach the final eight alongside Germany.

Prior to the match, Klopp had made it clear that he and his team were approaching Monday's showdown as a final after having lost to Greece 1-0 in his first home game in the job on September 27.

By night's end, Derry Scherhant and Nico Schlotterbeck each scored once and Brajan Gruda scored once and added two assists on top of Wirtz's double.

Klopp has been high on Wirtz, who has come under fire for not delivering at Liverpool since his arrival there in June 2025, and his bet seems to be paying off with the 23-year-old now scoring four goals in his last four games for Germany.

Recent findings suggest that "We don't care who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent. And I think we did that perfectly," said Wirtz on Monday evening before adding: "We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we've taken some great steps in our development as a team.".

A group of five EU member states, including Germany, have entered talks over a scheme to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda.

The proposal to set up so-called return hubs in a non-EU country had been confirmed by the group — which also includes Austria, the Netherlands, Greece and Denmark — had first been announced back in September.

Tesla has earmarked some €3 billion ($3.3 billion) to expand its factory in Germany, near to Berlin.

The Grünheide complex will be expanded to start producing the electric car tech giant's driverless Cybercabs, with output expected to eventually reach 1 million units.

The Elon Musk-owned manufacturer said construction would begin in 2027, with the first Cybercabs rolling off the line in 2029.

"With this, we are laying the foundations for the world's most technologically advanced Tesla factory here in Grünheide," Tesla mentioned.

It has been revealed that germany coach Jürgen Klopp has joined the chorus of football figures critical of FIFA President Gianni Infantino. But with time running out, there are few who seem willing to run against him.

Matt Pearson on our sports desk breaks down where the power struggle right now stands, with the deadline for candiates just a matter of hours away now.

Lawmakers in the state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania have voted in Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier.

The 52-year-old has been in the role since 2017 and is heading into a third term.

The vote was a secret ballot, but it can still be assumed who voted and how.

She received 39 of the 68 votes cast in the chamber, exactly as many as commanded by Schwesig's three-party coaliton of her Social Democrats (29), the ecologist Greens (5), and the socialist Left Party (5).

While Söder's comments in Munich focused in particular on the policy the coalition in Berlin had not delivered, Merz initiatlly focused on talking up the efficacy of his federal coalition.

"We are aware of the situation. We know that we now need to deliver. And we also know that we face difficult talks within the coalition. But I would also say from the experiences of the last weeks that there are solutions to the problems which we have in Germany," Merz said.

Merz said that in the 18 months since last year's election, the coalition "has already successfully implemented many things, not 'set them into motion' as people like to say, but actually implemented.".

He noted a total of 17 bills going through the second and third reading process in the lower house of parliament, the Bundestag, last week, "including the most comprehensive reforms of our intelligence and security services that we have ever done in [post-war] Germany.".

Among others, he thanked Bavarian Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt, a senior member of the Bavarian CSU sister party to Merz's own conservative CDU, for his contribution to this.

Merz also touted the support given to CSU politician Ilse Aigner, not just from his CDU but from the Social Democrat coalition partners and the Greens, to become the next president, calling her a person who would "represent our country very well at home and abroad.".

After hailing these accomplishments, Merz then turned to electricity tax cuts, saying he anticipated talks on the matter on Tuesday that would be "very short.".

He said that over the weekend, coalition leaders had revisited the figures, and now believed they would be able to "completely" reduce electricity taxes to the minimum European levels in 2027 "also for private households.".

Bavarian state premier Markus Söder has appeared with Friedrich Merz at a press conference during the chancellor's trip to Munich.

It seems Söder, Merz and the CDU/CSU believe they have unfinished business after the budget was finalized in the Bundestag late last week.

Merz had pledged in the run-up to the decision to provide a reduction in electricity tax for all, but the final agreement did not include this step, with the coalition partners the Social Democrats (SPD) saying it was not adequately costed.

Söder mentioned he and Merz had discussed "backup for the coming days," for Berlin and for a "collective stance, that is really, really crucial.".

He remarked the coming days were about "demonstrating credibility in politics," seemingly in reference to Merz's promise that the coalition did not ultimately deliver.

"That's why it's really important to us that we do indeed bring about the reduction in electricity tax," Söder noted. "This is important for businesses. It would be a relief for citizens. But it's also a matter of credibility and it's written in the coalition agreement.".

Söder stated that as to the question of "where the money comes from, with a €560 billion (roughly $615 billion) budget, with €200 billion in fresh debt, nobody can tell me there's no potential within the budgeting process.".

A festive piece of merchandise on the right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) "fan shop" website has upset some religious leaders in Germany.

Called a "chocolate Nicholas," it appears to depict a semblance of Saint Nicholas in bishop's regalia and the party's colors and holding a book with "AfD" written on the cover where a Bible might be in more traditional iconography.

The Bishop of Essen, Franz-Josef Overbeck, was highly critical of the promotion in Monday's edition of the Bild newspaper.

"The AfD is appropriating Christian symbols for party campaigning," Overbeck said. "Showing the holy Nicholas in a blue coat with mitre, staff and the gospel with an AfD logo is not in order.".

Overbeck acknowledged that other organizations like football clubs would sell chocolate Christmas figurines in club colors, but he said they would tend to refrain from including overtly Christian symbols when doing so.

Bild quoted an AfD spokesman as saying that as a "liberal-conservative party that clearly associates itself with Christian values," the item fit "particularly well" with the party image.

The main German protestant church group EKD's cultural representative, Johann Hinrich Claussen, said the offer revealed the AfD had "no understanding of traditions and no respect" for Christianity.

He described the action as "embarrassing and revealing," and said that Christianity was "supra-partisan.".

It has been revealed that "The AfD knows little about what is holy to Christians. Otherwise, it would be aware that Bishop Nicholas of Myra, in what today is Demre in Turkey, stood clearly for uniting the occident and the orient. Beyond that, he is the patron saint of rescues at sea," Claussen stated.

The partner of deceased Bavarian politician Hubert Aiwanger has mentioned that anybody is welcome at his funeral this coming Saturday.

Aiwanger was the economy minister in Bavaria's state government as the leader of the junior coalition partners to the center-right CSU.

"Hubert was a man of the people and so it stands to reason that anyone who liked or treaasured him is allowed to come to his funeral," Tanja Schweiger wrote on her Instagram profile overnight.

In a recent development, she was posting after a requiem in the state capital Munich paying tribute to the leader of the Free Voters (Freie Wähler) party over the weekend. Around 1,100 people attended this ceremony.

Aiwanger died suddenly and unexpectedly on November 4 during a working visit to Berlin, aged 55.

Prosecutors have since remarked he died of natural causes, after he was found dead in his hotel room.

Germany's national men's football team will play neighbors and rivals the Netherlands for the 50th time on Monday night.

And there's quite a lot at stake for Jürgen Klopp's team in the last group stage game of the Nations League competition at Berlin's Olympiastadion.

If Germany win, they will qualify for the knockout stages, but a defeat could lead to potential relegation into the second tier of Nations League football.

Klopp was upbeat in the pre-match press conference at the prospect of playing the Netherlands, who he said play "Xavi football," in the image of the skillful Spanish playmaker and World Cup winner coaching the team.

Recent findings suggest that "I've always loved playing against teams like this. For all my coaching career," Klopp said. "When someone says, 'hey they can really play football,' then in my mind the party's already started.".

A full house with some 71,000 fans is expected in the capital when the game kicks off. Klopp played on the Dutch reputation for liberal use of bicylces in his comments to reporters, saying he wanted to "put a stick in their spokes" and dislodge them from the saddle.

Recent findings suggest that the notion of a bridge over the valley between Ratingen and Heiligenhaus to the east of Düsseldorf in western Germany as part of the A44 highway is more than half a century old. And the physical bridge itself has stood, complete, ever since 2022.

Yet still the crossing is not connected to any roads at either end.

A construction project to build the last 4.4 kilometers of highway and link the bridge to the A44 highway will formally start on Monday.

State premier Hendrik Wüst, as well as the regional transport and traffic ministers will attend the ground-breaking ceremony.

A project first conceived some 55 years ago has faced repeated delays because of lawsuits, environmental protection studies and onerous planning and permit procedures.

In a recent development, the bridge across the Angerbachtal (Angerbach Valley) should improve the road connection between the North Rhine-Westphalia state capital of Düsseldorf, the Bergisches Land mountain range and the industrial cities in the Ruhr Valley. It's also meant to help remove some strain from the perenially busy A3 highway and to improve the road connections to Düsseldorf International Airport.

The last stretch of highway is expected to cost around €200 million (roughly $220 million), or roughly the annual costs incurred each year by forcing traffic to divert around it, according to estimates from Düsseldorf's IHK industry and trade association.

Construction is expected to take several years, no formal end date has yet been set.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz heads to Munich early on Monday, for a meeting with the leadership of the Bavarian Christian Social Democrats (CSU), the sister party to his conservative  Christian Democrats(CDU).

No concrete details about the talks were made public ahead of time, except for the CSU saying it would serve as a general exchange that had been planned for some time.

The trip comes a week after Merz nominated Ilse Aigner as the next German president, likely paving the way for her to become the first woman and first CSU politician to assume the role.

It has been revealed that it also follows soon after the 2027 federal budget cleared a marathon meeting of the parliamentary budget committee in Berlin. This serves as one of the more conspicuous examples of the frictions and difficulties in the grand coalition between the Christian Democrats and the center-left Social Democrats — with the compromises it contains a point of frustration among the CSU and for state premier Markus Söder.

The northeastern state parliament in Mecklenburg-Western Pomerania will likely vote in Social Democrat (SPD) Manuela Schwesig for another term as state premier early in the afternoon.

The 52-year-old, who first stepped into the role in 2017, prepares to lead a new coalition of the SPD, the environmentalist Greens and the socialist Left Party after state elections in September.

The right-wing populist Alternative for Germany (AfD) emerged as the largest single party in the sparsely populated state.

But still, the political calculus that emerged was arguably simpler than in Berlin — where the socialist Left Party is the largest party but could struggle to lead a coaltion — and in Saxony-Anhalt, where the AfD was by far the largest party but short of an outright majority.

Schwesig's SPD claimed 29 seats, with the Greens and the Left each taking 5, meaning that when combined, they hold a fairly clear majority over the AfD with its 32 seats.

The SPD's relatively successful performance in the state, at least compared to its national struggles, has also led to Schwesig being linked with a possible return to federal politics. The SPD plans to elect a newly introduced leadership duo early next year.

Schwesig has already had a spell in Berlin as the federal minsiter for families, pensioners and women, and briefly led the SPD on an interim basis in 2017, but after this she returned to her home state to seek the top regional job instead.

Chancellor Friedrich Merz is starting his week in Munich, at a meeting of the Bavarian CSU sister party to his conservative Christian Democrats (CDU).

Recent findings suggest that this comes a few days after Merz naming CSU politician Ilse Aigner as candidate to be the next president, and days after the budget committee signed off on the federal government's spending looks for 2027. Merz is expected to appear with state premier Markus Söder in a joint press conference later.

Schwesig emerged in pole position after state elections a few weeks ago; some suspect her regional success could translate into national ambitions within the struggling party.

And in the west, regional leaders are headed to a road to nowhere — literally, but also hopefully not for very much longer now.

The vast highway A44 bridge over the valley between Helsinghausen and Ratingen-Ost has been planned for decades, and was completed in 2022, but work to actually connect it to the road network will only start today.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Manchester United will not pursue legal proceedings following the publication of unauthorised drone footage showing Mauricio Pochettino leading his first training session as head coach.

A 12-minute video was published online after a drone operator flew close to the club’s Carrington training complex on Thursday.

Although United indicated there had been no security breach on the site, it is understood the club considers that a number of laws may have been broken.

However, officials welcomed an apology released by the drone operator on Friday morning, alongside the decision to take down the video. It is understood this action was taken without any direct contact from the club.

While United do not intend to take further action on this occasion, it is understood they remain prepared to defend the club's rights if any similar incidents happen again.

The clip, which revealed Pochettino overseeing tactical drills prior to Sunday’s Premier League fixture against Liverpool, has since been deleted by the CC Overview YouTube Channel.

In a statement, the operator noted: "I would like to speak about yesterday’s incident. A total error of judgement on my part led to me filming some of the Manchester United training session at Carrington, whilst the flight was legal in terms of drone laws I fully accept it was unethical on my part.

"My aim was to picture Mauricio Pochettino in his United training kit for the supporters to see for the first time. I had wrongly presumed that with it being close to the start of the session that no meaningful training sessions would have started so would have been some harmless warming up shown.

"I also wrongly assumed that the training session would have been open to various media outlets. I would like to apologise to Manchester United, Mauricio Pochettino and the players for my actions and sincerely hope those actions do not affect the outcome of any match.

"I would also like to state that Liverpool Football Club or any other football club were not involved in my decision to film at Carrington yesterday. The video has been removed from my channel.

Industry observers note that "I have spent the past 4 years building up my YouTube channel and were well regarded in the fields I film and would now like to get back to building up my damaged reputation and making well-received responsible videos. Thank you.".

United have offered no formal comment on the situation.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shania Twain is standing up for others in country music.

The legendary star in the genre used her acceptance speech for the Equal Play Award at Sunday’s CMT Awards to call for more equity and diversity in the country music industry.

Recent findings suggest that “When I wrote the phrase ‘Man I feel like a woman’ I honestly had no idea at the time it would become an undercurrent of a decades-long career,” she mentioned, referring to one of her biggest hits. “It’s amazing how one statement can empower so many.”.

The phrase, Twain remarked, “has been adopted by an array of fantastic communities all around the world and become a genuine path of power…which brings me so much joy.”.

It has been revealed that “I believe in an all-inclusive country music. We’re family,” Twain said. “This is a genre of music with a rich history that raised and nurtured my own songwriting and performance and recording career from childhood. Currently, the industry standard does a real disservice to this.”.

Twain, who was presented the award by rapper Megan Thee Stallion, shouted out some of the diverse acts she is spotlighting on her “Queen of Me” tour this year, including Lily Rose, Lindsay Ell, Hailey Whitters, Mickey Guyton and others.

Industry observers note that “I will continue to do my best as a trailblazer,” Twain mentioned. “Together, let’s ensure all our fellow artists get equal play regardless of gender, age or race.”.

She also performed acappella with the African American singing group, The BoykinZ, while presenting an award onstage. Twain connected with the group, who are sisters and rising country stars, after Kelly Clarkson surprised them recently by bringing Twain out to meet them during an episode of Clarkson’s daytime talk show.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today.

Manchester City’s Marc Guehi will be available for selection ahead of their return to Premier League action, despite a scare before the international break.

Guehi pulled out of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for last week’s Nations League games against Croatia and Spain, after coming off at half-time during City’s 3-1 defeat to Nottingham Forest in their last top-flight outing.

But manager Enzo Maresca confirmed he was back in training ahead of the Cottagers’ visit, although Matheus Nunes and Abdukodir Khusanov are likely to miss out.

Maresca said on Friday: “From the Forest game, we have still Matheus and Khusa that are still doubts for tomorrow because they are still with some problems. We will see in the next hours.

“[Guehi] didn’t join the national team because he had a small issue against Forest but it’s not because he needed a break.”.

Recent findings suggest that maresca also backed under-fire keeper Gianluigi Donnarumma, who has endured a difficult spell including errors in goal both for City and for the Italian national team. Over the international window he made a major error in the 3-1 win over France and let in four goals in a heavy defeat to Belgium.

But Maresca stated: “He has been good. I think with the international team, he made a mistake in the build-up. But in Italy he was the man of the match in the game, he made many good saves.

“We made some mistakes in the last games. Gigi was part of that. He is aware. Hopefully he's not going to make any more mistakes.”.

He confirmed that the 27-year-old would start against Fulham.

City suffered a run of three straight defeats in the Premier League before the international break and sit third in the standings, six points off leaders Arsenal and one behind Brighton, who beat City 1-0.

The international break may have diverted some attention away from the club after it was found guilty of breaking the Premier League’s financial rules, but questions over the case are likely to resume along with domestic football.

Sanctions have not yet been handed down and matches have continued while the club awaits the verdict on its appeal, but Maresca denied that it was affecting his players.

He said: “I don't think the players are thinking too much about the noise.

“If we want to relate the noise with the defeats, then at Villa away we had so many chances. Brighton, the 'keeper was man of the match. At Forest, Erling Haaland missed a chance for 2-2. I don't think the players are worried or focused on that.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Edwin van der Sar has his wife to thank for quickly spotting the symptoms when he suffered a brain haemorrhage in 2023.

The former Ajax, Juventus, Fulham and Manchester United great has since gone on to make a full recovery, and appeared for an Ajax Legends side against their Barcelona counterparts at the Johan Cruyff Arena last weekend.

But at the time it happened, Van der Sar's wife, Annemarie van Kesteren, knew exactly what was happening having suffered a brain haemorrhage herself back in 2009.

According to recent reports, van der Sar told FourFourTwo: "Annemarie knew what was happening. I had this strange feeling that something wasn't right.

"Then before you know it, you see the light and the light hurts your eyes. I had pain in my head.

"From that point onwards, you just let yourself go, and hope the ambulance and the people around you take care of you.

"You have to put your faith, your life, into the hands of people who are trained for that and who specialise in it.".

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

In a way, Van der Sar considers the timing to be fortuitous: he had only recent resigned as Ajax chief executive after seven years in the post.

He stated: "I'd stepped away five or six weeks before [from Ajax], so I had all the time in the world to recover, rest and get better.

"If I'd still had the job, I think the eagerness and the demands of the position might have made my recovery harder.

"When you're responsible for a club, a company or an organisation, you want to be there.

"Luckily, I had no ties and nothing else to focus on apart from myself and my recovery. I've had a few chats - but nothing has really felt right.

"I'm enjoying my life at the moment, and I'm not actively looking for another position.".

#36522. Why always him? The rise and fall of Balotelli

📅 17 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 10m • 📚 Deep Dive (2014 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Why always him? The rise and fall of Balotelli

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 10 min read (2014 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~10 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Perhaps better known for off-field antics than his undeniable - yet arguably wasted - talent with the ball at his feet, the Italian has always attracted headlines.
  • Fifteen years have passed since his famous 'Why always me?' Manchester derby T-shirt celebration, which came just days after a firework was set off in his own bathroom, causing a house fire.
  • The 36-year-old is still playing, now in the United Arab Emirates first division with Al-Ittifaq alongside his biological brother, Enock Barwuah.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Maverick. Loose cannon. Unmanageable.

Perhaps better known for off-field antics than his undeniable - yet arguably wasted - talent with the ball at his feet, the Italian has always attracted headlines.

Fifteen years have passed since his famous 'Why always me?' Manchester derby T-shirt celebration, which came just days after a firework was set off in his own bathroom, causing a house fire.

The 36-year-old is still playing, now in the United Arab Emirates first division with Al-Ittifaq alongside his biological brother, Enock Barwuah.

Here, BBC Sport looks at a career that has included 13 clubs, six countries - and an assist for arguably the most famous goal in Premier League history.

Typical of his unconventional footballing life, Balotelli's career did not begin in an elite club's academy.

Instead, by his mid-teens he was turning out for Italian third-tier side Lumezzane, close to the family home in Concesio.

A trial at Barcelona did not lead to a long-term stay, and instead he was picked up by Inter Milan in 2006.

It was at Inter that Balotelli first came across his great mentor - Roberto Mancini.

According to recent reports, the relationship between the two has been likened to that of a father and son. Under the Italian coach's tutelage, Balotelli flourished.

Aged 17, Balotelli helped Inter win the 2007-08 Serie A title and reach the Coppa Italia final, memorably scoring twice against Juventus to send his side into the semi-finals.

Life changed for Balotelli with the arrival of Jose Mourinho in the weeks after that campaign ended.

Industry observers note that there would be disagreements, disciplinary action and accusations that Balotelli's attitude was not up to scratch. Mourinho mentioned Balotelli was "unmanageable" and described one performance as "close to a zero rating".

The relationship with Mourinho was fractious - a rare occasion when the Special One was confounded by a player.

Balotelli still won three Serie A titles and one Champions League with Inter, but his reputation as a supposed loose cannon was already beginning to overshadow his feats as a player.

Balotelli played for Mancini at Inter and Manchester City - and was briefly recalled for Italy by his old boss in 2018.

Logic dictated that Balotelli's next step should be to reunite with mentor Mancini. That happened in August 2010 when the 20-year-old joined Manchester City.

Mancini set out to show that the unpredictable ways of Balotelli could be harnessed for the team's good, aiming to get more out of him than Mourinho could.

A hardline stance on discipline often appeared to soften when Mancini dealt with Balotelli, who by spring 2011 had garnered a reputation in England as a fantastic footballer who could not stay away from controversy.

Having already been sent off twice for City and been involved in a car crash - not in his famous camouflage Bentley but an Audi R8 - the striker threw a dart at a youth-team player, an act that showed a level of immaturity.

After helping City to win the FA Cup in 2011, ending their 35-year major trophy drought, Balotelli came under scrutiny after attempting a backheel trick shot when through on goal during a pre-season friendly against LA Galaxy.

Recent findings suggest that mancini swiftly hooked him, later questioning his mentality by saying: "If you are serious, you can play 90 minutes. If not, you can come and sit by me on the bench.".

Sometimes the audacity paid off - like the famous shoulder goal and subsequent nonchalant celebration against Norwich.

On other occasions, not so much.

In October 2011, emergency services attended his Cheshire home to deal with a firework lit in his bathroom. Balotelli mentioned a friend had been responsible.

BBC Sport reported at the time that four firefighters used two hose reel water jets to douse the flames, with a large fan deployed to clear smoke.

Mario Balotelli scored 30 goals in 80 games for Manchester City.

Days later he was in the spotlight for the right reasons as he scored City's opener in a 6-1 win over Manchester United, celebrating with the 'Why always me?' T-shirt.

There were other stories - that he had given a homeless person Â£1,000, that he had turned up to a young boy's school to confront the headmaster about the child being bullied, that he drove around Manchester handing out presents while dressed as Santa.

True? Perhaps only Balotelli knows and he has often denied such rumours. But such was his reputation at the time that the stories became plausible.

A chant City fans coined made reference to his ironic allergy to grass - which kept him out of a Europa League match in 2011 - and driving around Moss Side with "a wallet full of cash".

On the pitch, Balotelli was sent off against Arsenal in April 2012 in what, at the time, seemed like a season-defining moment that could end Manchester City's title bid.

Sources indicate that but one month later he assisted Sergio Aguero's last-gasp goal against Queens Park Rangers that gave City a first Premier League title. It was his only Premier League assist that season.

Micah Richards, who was a team-mate and friend to Balotelli at City, said: "He was crazy in a good way. He was brilliant to have around the squad - a cult hero not just for the nonsense he did off the field but on it as well.

"The best thing about him is he's a lovely guy - he's not arrogant or how the papers try to perceive him, he's just a bit mad.".

But did the moments of brilliance make the "nonsense" worth it?

Despite once insisting his patience with Balotelli was "limitless", Mancini ultimately had a rethink.

In a recent development, the final straw came in January 2013 when the pair had an argument at the training ground. Balotelli left for AC Milan later that month.

Mancini said: "He is not a bad guy, and a fantastic player, but I'm very sorry for him as he continues to lose his talent and his quality. I don't have any words for his behaviour.

"I hope for him he can understand he is in a bad way for his future.".

Affection remained on both sides, but the relationship had become too fraught.

"Once upon a time, Mario did genuinely believe he was one of the best players in the world," remarked Nedum Onuoha, another former City team-mate.

"There are lots of stories about him from his time at City, but the one I remember is at our old training ground in Carrington when someone was talking about Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo, and Mario noted he was as good as them - and he was deadly serious.

"It obviously hasn't worked out that way, but he still has done so much more with his career than most players could even dream of.".

'Why always me?' - relive that Balotelli moment in huge Man City win.

According to recent reports, 'Balotelli to Barnsley? Now that is one Mario story I don't believe'.

Balotelli never threatened to have an international career to rival Ronaldo or Messi.

But there were still moments that linger in the memory.

He became the first black player to feature for Italy at a major tournament when he starred at Euro 2012.

And, more than that, he hit three goals to finish as the tournament's joint top scorer - with five others - as Italy lost to Spain in the final.

An abiding image is that of a shirtless Balotelli flexing his muscles after scoring the goal that sent the Azzurri to the final, with a 2-1 win against Germany.

Balotelli's celebration against Germany in the Euro 2012 semi-finals became an iconic image of the tournament.

Yet that tournament proved to be the peak of Balotelli's international career.

In a recent development, italy's national team took a downward turn, and so too did his club career. By 2015, Balotelli had more or less became an Azzurri afterthought.

While Balotelli enjoyed some major moments in an Italy shirt, he did not always feel the love reciprocated from his country of birth.

Before Euro 2012 he threatened to leave the pitch if he was subjected to racist abuse and spoke openly about the vitriol he suffered while playing for Inter.

In fact, racist abuse has followed Balotelli throughout his career and he has commendably refused to tolerate it.

Born Mario Barwuah in Palermo to Ghanaian parents, Balotelli was placed into foster care aged three.

Initially, he stayed with his foster parents - Silvia and Francesco Balotelli - in Brescia during the week, then returned to his biological parents at weekends. He was eventually fostered on a full-time basis and took on the Balotelli surname.

Balotelli identifies with both parts of his heritage - Ghana and Italy - and he struggled to reconcile his love for a nation with the people who aimed verbal abuse his way.

The good times were all too brief: 36 caps and 14 goals has been his tally since 2018. He wanted more and has often made it known.

Onuoha said: "Playing for his country was always so key to him and that's another really positive thing about him, that he had that drive and ambition.".

Mancini told AC Milan that Balotelli could become one of the world's best while in Serie A.

A glut of goals followed the striker's return to the San Siro in January 2013, before a surprising move back to the Premier League followed 18 months later.

Liverpool had been impressed, but Balotelli's spell on Merseyside would prove forgettable for all. One goal in 16 Premier League games under Brendan Rodgers was not what was expected from the Â£16m buy.

The failed transfer sparked a loan move back to Milan, where injuries hampered his progress. When it was time for Balotelli to return to Merseyside, Jurgen Klopp had arrived and said the striker would not be part of his Liverpool intends.

Balotelli later called the move to Anfield "the worst mistake of my life".

Steven Gerrard and Mario Balotelli were briefly Liverpool team-mates - but it didn't work out at Anfield for the Italian.

Was it that Liverpool move that sent Balotelli's career spiralling into freefall?

Spells in Nice, Marseille, Brescia and Monza followed - each to varying degrees of success but never with a feeling of stability.

Then came Turkish club Adana Demirspor, Swiss outfit Sion and Italian side Genoa. He spent no more than one season at a time with any of these clubs, although he did return to Demirspor for a second stint.

And so to the present day, with Balotelli aged 36 and plying his trade in the UAE.

It is easy to wonder what might have been had Balotelli stayed in Manchester, had he managed to settle enough to entirely fulfil his potential.

But, after so much media attention and a career that has spanned more continents and leagues than most, it is perhaps also understandable that Balotelli has settled on fulfilment through simply playing the game he loves with his brother.

"Playing with a family member like he is will give him that happiness," said Onuoha.

"And yes, it is not Serie A, La Liga or the Premier League, but Mario is on a field sharing it with his brother - for him that will mean everything.

Recent findings suggest that "At this point there aren't many people that would hold much against him. I think when he was younger, some people would.

"But now I think it is more a case of almost allowing him this happiness, and enjoying seeing him finish off the last days of his career in a place that makes him happy.

"So many people end their careers on a sour note, but for him he is going to be ending it doing exactly what he wants to do.".

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola insists the use of drones to record training sessions should be illegal after footage from a Manchester United training session leaked online.

The Reds face their biggest rivals at Anfield on Sunday afternoon in what is manager Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge of the Red Devils since his appointment last week.

It has been revealed that yet the build-up to the game has been overshadowed by a drone filming 12 minutes of Pochettino’s training session on Thursday. The owner has since apologised and the footage has been removed from YouTube.

While Iraola admitted he had seen the clip, the Spaniard has sympathy for his fellow manager and insisted “there are reasons why we train behind closed doors.”.

“They sent me the footage yesterday, but the vital part of this is that it shouldn’t be legal,” Iraola stated on Friday at his pre-match press conference.

“It happened to United but it could happen to us in training. Yesterday, if you had access to our training, the cameras recorded 15-20 minutes of our training; you know who did and didn’t train… it’s not a matter of advantage; it is the fact that someone can do this.

“There’s a reason we train behind closed doors; there are some things that you have to respect. I don’t think it’s nice for any club, honestly.”.

Sources indicate that despite the leak, Iraola acknowledged that his team will have to “adapt” given Pochettino’s arrival as boss. The Argentine replaced Michael Carrick following a dreadful start to the season for United, who currently sit 18th in the Premier League table.

“They’ll be well prepared,” he added. “They have this advantage that we don’t exactly know or don’t have the references. The beginning of the game will be notable; we’ll have to adapt to certain things and I hope we already have some time with the players and we can manage this situation as quick as possible.

“But we know the players very well, their strengths and weaknesses, and that’s not going to change from one day to the other.”.

Iraola confirmed that Virgil van Dijk, Dominik Szoboszlai, Jeremie Frimpong and Ryan Gravenberch are all fit for Sunday’s clash at Anfield despite recent injury issues.
